newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack shares extend recent gains.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack shares extend recent gains.

text.p: Shares in Britain's newly privatised rail operator Railtrack extended recent gains on Friday amid talk of continued U.S. interest in the partly paid stock, dealers and analysts said.
"There are certainly a few buyers out there at low levels," said one dealer.
"It's all old news, there are no fundamental changes," he said in reference to talk about upward revision of the company's property portfolio.
Railtrack stock was up 1/2p at 285p at 1041 GMT, on more than 5.4 million shares traded after earlier touching 291p.
"We have only seen buyers recently," said another dealer, adding that all the interest was from U.S. investors.

One analyst, who asked not to be named, said dealers' interest was fuelled by speculation about the value of Railtrack's property holdings and by its better-than-expected performance in relation to government financial targets.

"It's the partly-paid nature of the share, the query about property valuations and the relatively good performance. The shares are part paid so there's the yield performance effect...It's still not terribly expensive."
Analyst David Myrddin-Evans of Keinwort Benson disagreed, saying interest was overblown.
"There's no real reason for it to be up. There are a lot of rumours there at the moment but if you put it all together and think about it doesn't stand up," he said.
Railtrack would take any performance bonus as a provision "for a rainy day", Myrddin-Evans said, meaning that it would not feed through to any profit figure.
He was also sceptical about any benefits from revised property values or about under-valuation of the partly-paid stock.
"Whether it's partly paid or not it's still expensive. We regard it as being overpriced at the moment," he said.
